newsitem.title: GERMANY: German feed industry ready to use more grain.
newsitem.headline: German feed industry ready to use more grain.

text.p: Grain use in German compound feed is likely to rise in 1997 after sharp gains in 1996.

"I see further advances in grain inclusion as more domestic grain becomes available from the 1996 and 1997 crops," Manfred Schraeder, president of feeds industry association FFMI, told a news conference on Thursday.
Schraeder cited relatively low grain prices versus other energy-rich feed ingredients and an overall rise in compound feed output by 2.4 percent to 19.33 million tonnes last year.
Grain use in the 1996 feed total rose by 15 percent to 6.6 million tonnes.
Grain accounted for 34.1 percent of the raw materials used in compound feed after 30.4 percent in 1995.
Oilmeal use last year dropped to 4.76 million tonnes from 4.88 million in 1995, representing 24.6 percent (25.9).
Grain use was underpinned by European Union policy, which encouraged domestic consumption, Schraeder said.
The industry was grappling with high prices of imported protein feeds led by soy meal, where the firm dollar versus the mark added to importers' costs.
Schraeder said world protein markets were set to remain tight because Asian demand was expanding fast and feed was being diverted from Europe to countries like China.
"Perhaps we will soon move away from farm surplus fears in Europe and see zero land set-aside if global food demand keeps rising at the current pace," he said.
In some cases, the industry had benefited from price strength in the soy complex.
Schraeder explained that farmers had turned away from on-farm mixing of grains with expensive bulk soy and instead bought compound feed from industrial plants.
Total German feed use of grains exceeded 20 million tonnes a year if direct on-farm feeding was included.
